title: The Slow Archive
premise: Sable Yarrow, a terraformer hauling seed-cargo through contested orbits, intercepts a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct for two centuries — a language preserved only in the Slow Archive, a garden-ship's genetic memory she helped build. The signal comes from a penal relay where survivors of an illegal Earth purge have been erased from every record, and Earth's last transmission loop will overwrite them forever when it ends. Racing a rival salvager who wants the relay's salvage rights and a magistrate who wants the erasure buried, Sable must choose between her contract, her crew, and broadcasting the truth. In the end she reaches the relay, loses her ship, and seeds the archive with the survivors' testimony — justice delivered not by law, but by memory outliving the law's silence.
about_author: Beatrix Marchetti is a former botanical archivist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds before turning to fiction. She writes slow-burning science fiction about people who tend things — gardens, records, grudges — longer than anyone expects to matter.

chapters.title: Seed Cargo
chapters.summary: Sable Yarrow's POV. She ferries dormant seed-vaults through contested orbits, logging a routine day that establishes her contract with the Terraforming Consortium, her debt, and her quiet habit of talking to plants no one will see bloom for a century. Beat: loneliness disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Language That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A distress signal arrives in Vessic, a dead tongue Sable knows only because she catalogued its seed-names. She verifies it isn't a ghost echo — it's repeating, and it's recent. Beat: the thrill and dread of an impossible message.

chapters.title: Crew of Convenience
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with engineer Dov Okonkwo and navigator Ilsa Reyes. She tells them nothing, but they notice the course change. Dov warns that deviating voids their salvage bond. Beat: loyalty tested by a secret not yet spoken.

chapters.title: What the Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She decrypts the signal using the Slow Archive's linguistic seed-index and learns it originates from Relay Kestrel-9, officially decommissioned and legally nonexistent. Beat: the first hard fact — the signal is a plea from people erased.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Magistrate Corven Hale hails her ship: return the intercept, take amnesty and debt forgiveness. He speaks of the transmission loop ending in nineteen days. Sable stalls. Beat: temptation with a polite face.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Sable confesses everything to Dov and Ilsa. Dov wants the amnesty; Ilsa, a former archivist herself, wants the truth. They vote — barely — to divert. Beat: a crew becoming a conspiracy.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The rival salvager Vasko Tarn shadows them, having intercepted Hale's broadcast. A tense docking-approach standoff at a fuel depot ends in a grudging, temporary truce. Beat: the enemy who might become an ally, or worse.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Entering the relay's dead zone, all navigation fails except dead-reckoning. Ilsa narrates her own past erasure from records after a union strike. Beat: personal history rhyming with the mission.

chapters.title: The First Survivor
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A half-broken escape pod carries a dying woman, Miret, who speaks Vessic. She reveals the purge: four hundred dissidents dumped at Kestrel-9, their identities overwritten in Earth's master loop. Beat: the abstract becomes a face.

chapters.title: Miret's Testimony
chapters.summary: Miret's POV. In the medbay she records her account — names, dates, the magistrate who signed the erasure order: Hale's own mentor, and Hale's signature as witness. Beat: the horror of complicity by paperwork.

chapters.title: Tarn's Price
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Tarn offers to escort them through a debris field in exchange for the salvage rights to Kestrel-9's hull. Dov, pragmatic, wants to accept. Sable refuses. Beat: the crew fractures over what justice costs.

chapters.title: The Debris Field
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They attempt the crossing without Tarn and lose their cargo bay — the seed-vaults — to a micrometeor swarm. Sable grieves the garden meant for the unborn. Beat: sacrifice of the future to save the past.

chapters.title: Hale's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hale broadcasts a warrant: Sable is now officially a pirate. He reveals the loop ends in six days, and any broadcast from Kestrel-9 will be legally classified as noise. Beat: the law weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. They reach the relay: rusted, cold, but alive. Two hundred survivors remain, rationing air, maintaining the signal by hand for three years. Beat: awe and grief — the archive of the living.

chapters.title: The Elder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The survivors' elder, Ansem, refuses rescue: they will not leave until their names are restored. Sable proposes the impossible — broadcast the testimony through the Slow Archive's seed-index, hidden inside legal agricultural telemetry. Beat: hope built from a loophole.

chapters.title: Tarn Returns
chapters.summary: Tarn's POV. Tarn arrives, tipped off by Hale, to claim salvage — and finds people, not salvage. His own sister was erased in a similar purge. Beat: the mercenary's conversion, earned not given.

chapters.title: The Loop Begins to Close
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Earth's final overwrite transmission begins, and every relay in range starts purging legacy data. Dov rigs the archive uplink while the ship's systems fail around him. Beat: engineering as resistance against the clock.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The testimony goes out woven through seed-telemetry — four hundred names planted in the one record Earth never purges: its food supply. Hale's jamming fleet arrives. Beat: the climax's first strike — truth released.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. To hold the transmission open, Sable vents her ship — her home, her debt collateral, her only asset. Tarn's vessel shields the relay from Hale's guns and is destroyed; Tarn survives, broken. Beat: the price of survival, paid in full.

chapters.title: Hale's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The names surface in every granary manifest on Earth; the erasure is undeniable. Hale, facing inquiry, chooses to testify against his mentor rather than bury it again. Beat: the antagonist's redemption through paperwork turned against its makers.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The survivors are legally restored and offered transport home. Ansem asks Sable to stay and help rebuild the relay as a free archive. Miret's recording plays over the docking bay. Beat: grief and relief braided together.

chapters.title: The Slow Archive
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. A year later, Sable tends the relay-garden where the seed-vaults' twins now grow — a garden for the living and the remembered. She plants the first Vessic seed and speaks a name aloud. Beat: quiet resolution — justice as something tended, not won.
